significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that, across the stated laws, a physical scalar maps "monotonically and log-linearly onto a low-dimensional representational axis" with a slope matching the scientific exponent, and that exponent distortion predicts extrapolation error; this constrains expected internal geometry and out-of-distribution behavior rather than merely asserting concept decodability. It would establish a quantitative representational phenomenon, but not a causal mechanism, and its value is supported by the role of analytic-law recovery in work such as Cranmer et al.'s "Discovering Symbolic Models from Deep Learning with Inductive Biases" (NeurIPS 2020). The branches are distinguishable through exponent fidelity and its error coupling, although a negative result would rule out only this linear/transformed-coordinate encoding and not scientific internalization generally, while the phrase "true scientific understanding versus curve-fitting" remains underdetermined. Topic substitution does not preserve the score: the assigned topic alone does not imply exponent recovery or the proposed predictive coupling, so the claim adds a materially stronger quantitative law above the median concept-probing hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Scaling Fidelity Score" and "dimensional-consistency test," which could be used to audit a model's quantitative physical consistency and, if the claimed link holds, flag extrapolation risk before deployment rather than merely explain an observed failure. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives calibration: the recovered relation should have the textbook exponent and deviations should couple to out-of-distribution errors, although the claim concedes that findings may remain "model- and law-specific." The asserted scope spans several model classes and scientific domains, with likely uptake by scientific-model developers and auditors, but use requires a known law and suitable controlled inputs and thus is not a general-purpose deployment screen. Topic substitution would leave only generic representation auditing and would not earn this score; the transferable exponent/error relation and explicit metrics are the claim-specific sources of reach.
